# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | white |
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| white | blue |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: My touch view shows five wire positions but no distinguishing tactile information yet. Please relay the manual rule once you identify what visible details it needs.

I need transmit the manual’s color-to-color mapping to Deaf, who can see both the light and wire colors and can then tell Blind which wire to cut. I will use visible finger-count pairs as indices in the conventional order red, yellow, green, blue, white: 1→2, 2→3, 3→1, 4→5, 5→4. Claps separate mapping pairs.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","✌","👏","✌","🤟","👏","🤟","☝","👏","🖖","🖐","👏","🖐","🖖"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | white |
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| white | blue |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb view: display 0; light yellow; wires in order 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. Mute, I received your gestures but do not know their code; please establish their meaning or use spoken relay through Blind if needed.
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display 0; light yellow; wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. Please determine the required cut from the manual and tell me its wire position in words.

The yellow light requires cutting the green wire. Deaf’s reported ordering places green at position 2. Since Blind needs a spoken position, I will make the clearly countable two-finger gesture to Deaf; Deaf can interpret it as wire position two and immediately relay that in words to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | white |
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| white | blue |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind: do not operate anything yet. Mute: I cannot decode the prior gestures. Use this protocol for a wire instruction: 👍 means CUT, then ☝ wire 1, ✌ wire 2, 🤟 wire 3, 🖐 wire 4, ✋ wire 5. 👎 means the manual requires another control; then gesture a simple description/code and I will establish more. Please resend the required action with this protocol.
Blind says to Mute: I cannot see Deaf's gesture protocol. Please answer me in spoken words with the manual's required action and wire number. Configuration: display 0, yellow light; wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red.

The manual says yellow light requires cutting green, and green is wire 2. Deaf has now established a visible protocol that I can use, and Deaf can relay the resulting instruction verbally to Blind after this turn.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","✌"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | white |
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| white | blue |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The prior instruction was successfully relayed and executed, and the bomb has changed. I need the updated visible and tactile information before determining any further manual instruction.

``` 
wait()
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | white |
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| white | blue |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Correct: wire 2 was cut and the bomb changed. New view: display 0; light blue; wires 1 yellow, 2 CUT, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 white. Blind: wait for Mute's next instruction.
Blind says to Mute: Stage update from Deaf: display 0; light blue; wires 1 yellow, 2 already cut, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 white. Please consult the manual and tell me the next required action and wire number in spoken words.

A blue light requires cutting the white wire. In the updated wire order, white is position 5. I will use Deaf’s established CUT-plus-position protocol so Deaf can relay the instruction verbally to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","✋"])
```
